title: How to Choose a Payment Gateway in India at ₹50 Lakh Monthly Revenue: Pricing and ROI in 2026
summary: Compare payment gateway pricing at ₹50 lakh monthly GMV in India. Explore Razorpay custom quotes, credit-card fees and ROI at ₹1 crore and ₹10 crore volumes.
body_markdown:
A payment gateway connects your checkout to payment networks and helps you collect customer payments. At ₹50 lakh in monthly payment GMV, choosing one means comparing negotiated fees, successful collections, and operating costs. **Razorpay is worth shortlisting** because its[public pricing page](https://razorpay.com/pricing/) invites custom-pricing discussions for businesses accepting over ₹5 lakh per month. At your volume, request a written, method-wise proposal and compare it against your actual payment data.


The right choice depends on your credit-card and UPI mix, refund rate, settlement requirements, and checkout performance. A lower quoted percentage can save money, but the comparison changes if more customers complete their payments or your team spends less time reconciling transactions.


Throughout this guide, ₹50 lakh means monthly payment value processed through your gateway. Business revenue and payment GMV can differ because of COD, offline collections, refunds, and other channels. Use gateway data when negotiating pricing and unique attempted payment value when measuring payment completion.


## Key Takeaways


- At ₹50 lakh monthly payment GMV, ask Razorpay for a custom proposal rather than assuming the public headline rate is your final quote.
- Compare fees using successfully captured payment value and your actual method mix.
- Recovered collections are additional sales, not additional profit. Apply contribution margin before calculating ROI.
- On ₹50 lakh of unique attempted payment value, a one-percentage-point increase in value-based completion adds ₹50,000 in captured payments.
- Price settlement delays using net daily receipts and your actual annual funding rate.
- Include refunds, disputes, fixed fees and applicable taxes without counting the same cost twice.
- Verify the contracting entity’s applicable RBI authorisation and record commercial terms in writing.


## Can You Negotiate Razorpay Pricing at ₹50 Lakh Monthly GMV?


Yes, you can request a custom-pricing discussion: Razorpay’s public pricing page explicitly invites businesses accepting over ₹5 lakh per month to get in touch. ₹50 lakh exceeds that published enquiry threshold. It does not guarantee a particular discount, enterprise designation, or settlement arrangement.


The proposal should reflect your successful payment value, transaction count, average ticket size, business category, risk profile, and instrument mix. Ask for separate domestic consumer credit-card, corporate or premium-card, debit-card, UPI, netbanking and international-payment terms. A blended quote alone cannot tell you your credit-card rate.


Get refund-fee treatment, dispute charges, settlement fees, optional products, minimum commitments, support arrangements, rate-review dates and exit clauses in the same document. Confirm whether taxes are included. The[Razorpay Payment Gateway](https://razorpay.com/payment-gateway/) product page explains the collection platform; the commercial proposal determines your actual costs.


### What to Request in Your Custom Quote


Method-wise pricing and contract checklist Cost or term What to request from Razorpay How it enters ROI

## The Five Inputs for Calculating Payment Gateway Cost


**Net collections after payment costs = captured payment value − refunds − unrecovered dispute losses − processing fees − applicable taxes − fixed payment costs.** Calculate settlement financing separately. This collections figure is not business profit: product, fulfilment, and other operating costs still apply.


### 1. Payment Method Mix and Blended Fees


**Blended processing rate = total percentage-based processing fees ÷ successful payment value.** Equivalently, weight each method’s rate by its share of successful payment value. Keep fixed per-transaction fees separate. Use 90 days of data so a change in card or UPI share does not masquerade as a better negotiated rate.


> **Did You Know?** A low blended rate can coexist with a higher credit-card rate when much of your payment value comes from lower-cost methods. Ask for both figures.


### 2. Payment Completion


For this ROI model, **value-based payment completion = successfully captured value ÷ unique attempted payment value × 100** . Deduplicate orders and retries. Track first-attempt success separately from eventual payment completion, and keep capture separate from settlement.


Compare matching methods, issuers, ticket sizes and customer cohorts. Include technical declines, customer authentication failures and retry recovery. A provider-wide benchmark cannot establish the improvement your business will receive.


### 3. Fixed Fees and Taxes


Divide annual maintenance fees by 12 for a monthly comparison. List recurring technology, reconciliation, and other product charges separately. Record setup and migration expenditure as one-off costs for payback; do not also deduct their full value as monthly recurring costs.


Where a processing fee attracts 18% GST, a 2% fee produces a 2.36% cash deduction before other charges. Calculate GST on taxable fees, not the customer’s entire purchase value. Confirm applicable invoice treatment and input-tax-credit eligibility with your finance team. Recoverable tax and cash paid are different measures.


### 4. Settlement Delay and Funding Cost


**Additional settlement float = average daily net receipts × extra settlement-delay days.** Approximate monthly financing cost as additional float × annual funding rate ÷ 12. Use actual settlement dates, cut-offs, holidays, reserves and holds.


Illustration: ₹50 lakh of monthly net receipts spread over 30 days is ₹1,66,666.67 per day. One extra day of delay ties up that amount. At an illustrative 15% annual funding rate, this costs approximately **₹25,000 annually, or ₹2,083.33 monthly** . Your net receipts and borrowing terms determine the real figure.


> **Pro-Tip:** Compare a faster-settlement fee against the financing saving on funds actually released earlier. Faster access does not automatically improve ROI.


### 5. Refunds, Disputes and Retained Fees


Ask whether original processing fees are returned after a refund. Retained refund-related processing fees equal refunded captured value × the applicable retained rate. If captured value is ₹50 lakh, refunds are 12% and the retained fee is 2%, the allocation is ₹12,000 before tax. These fees are already included if your model counts processing fees on all captured payments; do not subtract them again.


For disputes, model unrecovered principal, dispute fees and handling costs, less recoveries. Avoid counting the same reversed payment as both a refund and a dispute loss.


## How Razorpay’s Pricing and Welcome Offer Fit Your ROI


Razorpay’s public pricing page shows a 2% headline baseline and a custom-pricing enquiry option. At ₹50 lakh monthly GMV, model the ongoing written quote, including instrument-specific exceptions and applicable taxes. Introductory savings should be shown separately from recurring costs.


### What the 90-Day Welcome Offer Covers


The[official offer terms](https://razorpay.com/terms/90-day-free-pg-offer/) govern eligibility and exclusions. The benefit is a waiver of the platform fee on eligible domestic Payment Gateway transactions, subject to the following limits.


Welcome-offer limits to include in your model Term Scope


Eligibility Eligible new accounts activated on or after 1 July 2026; existing accounts transacting before that date are excluded


Maximum coverage 90 days from activation or ₹5,00,000 cumulative eligible transaction value, whichever is earlier


Excluded methods Prepaid cards, corporate credit cards, Amex, Diners Club and EMI-based methods


Other costs GST and statutory levies are not waived; a ₹199 KYC processing charge plus tax may apply


Account limits One benefit per PAN or bank account; only the first activated MID qualifies; unused credits expire


Fair use Razorpay may withdraw the benefit under fair-use terms, including where credit cards exceed 90% of volume


> **Did You Know?** ₹5 lakh in Amount Credits refers to covered eligible transaction value, not ₹5 lakh of processing-fee savings. It does not cover an entire ₹50 lakh month.


### Test Payment Recovery and Settlement on Your Own Traffic


Evaluate features such as[Razorpay SR Boosters](https://razorpay.com/blog/razorpay-sr-boosters-turn-failed-card-payments-into-found-revenue) in a controlled pilot. Measure incremental recovered payments, fees and contribution profit by issuer and payment method. Treat advertised feature benefits as hypotheses to test rather than a guaranteed success-rate uplift.


For[Instant Settlements](https://razorpay.com/blog/instant-settlement-payment-gateway) , confirm eligibility, release limits, availability and fees in writing. Compare actual settlement timing and funding savings against those charges.


## How to Model the UPI MDR Framework Effective 15 October 2026


As of this article’s 7 October 2026 review, the Department of Financial Services’ official MDR FAQs state that the selective UPI P2M framework takes effect on **15 October 2026** . It is not a blanket fee on every UPI payment.


Under the standard applicable category, P2M transactions above ₹2,000 attract 0.4%, capped at ₹300 per transaction at ₹75,000 and above. Payments up to ₹2,000 and qualifying small merchants are exempt. Specified merchant categories have different treatment. Confirm your classification and implementation with the acquiring provider.


Illustration: if ₹15 lakh consists entirely of eligible standard-category payments above ₹2,000, with each below ₹75,000 and no exemption, 0.4% is ₹6,000 before applicable tax. Do not apply this amount to all UPI value. For a qualifying ₹5 lakh transaction, the ₹300 cap gives an effective rate of 0.06%.


Keep bank-account UPI, credit-card-linked UPI, and prepaid or wallet-funded flows separate. Ask which network charges and gateway service fees apply to each. Recheck the official framework before publication and whenever pricing is reviewed.


## Can a Higher Processing Rate Deliver Better ROI?


Yes, if the contribution profit from additional completed payments and operating savings exceeds the extra cost. The following figures are **illustrative assumptions, not measured performance or quoted tariffs for any provider** . Both options receive ₹50 lakh of unique attempted payment value.


Illustrative monthly collections comparison Line item Option A Option B


Processing fee 1.75% 2.00%


Value-based completion 85% 93%


Captured payment value ₹42,50,000 ₹46,50,000


Processing fees ₹74,375 ₹93,000


GST at 18% on processing fees ₹13,387.50 ₹16,740


Monthly AMC allocation ₹416.58 (₹4,999 ÷ 12) ₹0


Collections after listed charges ₹41,61,820.92 ₹45,40,260


This table excludes refunds, disputes, financing, other fees and tax on AMC. Rounded monthly AMC is shown. Option B collects ₹3,78,439.08 more after the listed charges, but that difference is not profit.


At an illustrative 20% contribution margin before payment-processing costs, ₹4 lakh in additional captured sales contributes ₹80,000. Subtract the additional ₹21,977.50 in processing fees and GST, and add ₹416.58 saved AMC: the monthly benefit is **₹58,439.08 before other differences** . If GST is recoverable, calculate economic benefit separately from cash movement.


> **Pro-Tip:** There is no universal success-rate gap at which you should stop negotiating fees. Compare incremental contribution profit and costs using your own margins.


## Verify the Entity, Settlement Terms and Migration Economics


Check the exact legal entity contracting with you against RBI’s published authorisation or application-status records for the service being supplied. Distinguish final authorisation from an application or in-principle status. Request current evidence of applicable PCI DSS compliance, merchant KYC procedures and fund-handling arrangements.


Record settlement cycles, cut-offs, holidays, reserve or hold conditions, dispute procedures and escalation contacts. Do not assume a universal T+1 entitlement. For international collections, verify the relevant cross-border entity, service scope, supported flows, FX treatment and written pricing separately.


### Calculate Switching Payback


**Monthly net benefit = additional contribution profit + operating savings − incremental recurring costs.** Include fee differences once. **Payback in months = one-off migration cost ÷ positive monthly net benefit.** If monthly benefit is zero or negative, this model gives no positive payback.


Estimate integration, checkout testing, reconciliation changes, saved-card and mandate continuity, training and rollback effort for your actual setup. For illustration, a four-percentage-point completion gain on ₹50 lakh of unique attempted value adds ₹2 lakh in captured sales. At 20% contribution margin, that is ₹40,000 before incremental payment costs. If the final monthly net benefit is ₹30,000 and migration costs ₹60,000, payback is two months.


> **Pro-Tip:** Test saved-card and recurring-mandate continuity with returning customers before moving all traffic. Confirm what must be re-established during migration.


## Gateway Priorities for SaaS, D2C and Marketplaces


For SaaS, evaluate mandate registration, renewal completion and retry recovery separately.[Razorpay Subscriptions](https://razorpay.com/subscriptions/) is relevant to recurring collections; verify current method, category and authentication limits rather than assuming one threshold covers every mandate.


For D2C, compare checkout completion, payment recovery, and the contribution margin on additional delivered orders. Include your own COD and return-to-origin costs without attributing every improvement to the gateway. For marketplaces, measure vendor-settlement requirements, payout charges, and reconciliation hours, as well as checkout performance.


## What Changes at ₹1 Crore and ₹10 Crore Monthly GMV?


At ₹1 crore or over ₹10 crore monthly GMV, ask for a written volume-pricing schedule and service proposal. The relevant questions are whether slabs are automatic or require renegotiation, whether a rate applies to all qualifying volume or only the marginal tier, and how commitments, shortfalls and review dates work. These volumes do not establish a universal published card tariff.


For credit-card pricing specifically, separate total gateway GMV from successful credit-card GMV. Request distinct consumer, corporate, premium, EMI and international-card terms. A ₹1 crore blended portfolio can have much less than ₹1 crore of card payments. A ₹10 crore commitment should define measurement periods, eligible methods, refunds and failed-payment treatment.


Use the[₹1 crore pricing-renegotiation guide](https://razorpay.com/blog/renegotiate-payment-gateway-pricing-1-crore-gmv-india/) and[enterprise volume-pricing guide](https://razorpay.com/blog/enterprise-payment-gateway-pricing-volume-tiers-india/) to prepare your questions. Your signed method-wise proposal remains the source for actual rates.


## A Step-by-Step Framework for Choosing Your Gateway


1. Export 90 days of attempted and captured payments, deduplicating orders and segmenting methods, issuers and ticket sizes.
2. Build a monthly cost model with fees, refunds, disputes, fixed costs, financing and taxes. Apply UPI categories, exemptions, caps and effective dates correctly.
3. Request a written Razorpay custom proposal and comparable alternatives using the same volume and instrument assumptions.
4. Verify the contracting entity, compliance evidence, settlement terms, and service escalation process.
5. Run a controlled pilot across comparable customer cohorts. Measure recovery and contribution profit; show introductory savings separately.
6. Calculate payback, test migration continuity, and review commitments before signing or moving all traffic.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Does Razorpay offer custom pricing at ₹50 lakh monthly GMV?


Razorpay’s public pricing page invites custom-pricing discussions for businesses accepting over ₹5 lakh per month. At ₹50 lakh, request a written proposal; your rate depends on the assessed payment mix and commercial terms.


### What data should I share for a credit-card pricing quote?


Share 90 days of successful card payment value, transaction count, average ticket size, refunds and disputes. Split domestic consumer, corporate, premium, EMI and international cards. Specify total gateway GMV separately.


### Can a higher processing rate deliver better ROI?


Yes, when measured additional contribution profit and operating savings exceed extra fees and other costs. Apply your margin to recovered sales and compare matching cohorts before deciding.


### Does the 90-day offer cover my entire ₹50 lakh month?


No. Eligible coverage ends after 90 days or ₹5 lakh in cumulative eligible transaction value, whichever is earlier. Method exclusions, other charges and fair-use conditions also apply.


### Should I use multiple gateways at ₹50 lakh monthly GMV?


Assess resilience and payment recovery against extra integration, fees and reconciliation work. There is no universal GMV threshold.[Razorpay Optimizer](https://razorpay.com/optimizer-intelligent-payments-routing/) is relevant when evaluating routing across gateways; measure the net benefit for your traffic.
